newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rebels' mother fears for son's life.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebels' mother fears for son's life.

text.p: The mother of the guerrilla leader holding 83 VIP hostages in the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima said on Monday that she feared for her son's life and was worried the hostage crisis might end in bloodshed.

"As a mother I am very worried about my son ... My greatest concern is that there should not be a bloodbath," Felicita Cartolini, mother of Peruvian rebel leader Nestor Cerpa Cartolini, said in a joint interview from Paris with Reuters television and Peru's Channel Nine network.
Cerpa and about 20 heavily armed Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels stormed a lavish reception at the residence on Dec. 17 and took hundreds of guests hostage.
The MRTA rebels have booby-trapped and mined the residence against possible attack but Cerpa's mother, who lives in France, said she did not believe he would harm his captives.
"I know the human side of my son and I believe he will respect all of the hostages ... I don't think he is violent at the moment," she said.

The guerrillas have released at least 420 hostages since the crisis began. Cerpa held his first face-to-face talks with the Peruvian government's chief negotiator in the crisis -- Education Minister Domingo Palermo -- on Saturday, raising hopes that the crisis would end peacefully.
Cerpa's mother said she moved to France in 1988, fearing that police would use her to get to her son -- one of Peru's two most wanted men. She looks after Cerpa's two children.
Cartolini said Cerpa had probably stormed the embassy to draw attention to prison conditions faced by his jailed MRTA comrades.
"Maybe he has done this to pressure those who are inside -- authorities and diplomats -- so that there is justice because there are many injustices in the prisons," she said.
Cerpa and his comrades still hold the brother of Peru's President Alberto Fujimori, scores of top government officials, three ambassadors and dozens of Japanese businessmen.
